Use the canonical presentation
\[
S \simeq_R R[X]/(f)=\operatorname{AdjoinRoot}(f),
\]
under which `h.root` corresponds to `AdjoinRoot.root`. The key mechanism is the universal property: a morphism from an adjoin-root algebra is determined by its action on the coefficient ring and on the distinguished root.

Organize the argument around two facts:

1. `h.adjoinRootAlgEquiv` sends `AdjoinRoot.root` to `h.root`, so its inverse sends `h.root` back to the canonical root.

2. Extensionality for adjoin-root algebras: two algebra/ring homomorphisms agreeing on coefficients and on the distinguished root are equal.

The first fact and extensionality show that the canonical equivalence between two realizations \(S\) and \(T\) factors as
\[
S \xrightarrow{\,(\text{canonical } \operatorname{AdjoinRoot}(f)\to S)^{-1}\,}
\operatorname{AdjoinRoot}(f)
\xrightarrow{\,\text{canonical } \operatorname{AdjoinRoot}(f)\to T\,} T,
\]
giving both sides of the first `Iff`.

For the second `Iff`, apply the same uniqueness principle: the hypotheses `hmap` and `hroot` say exactly that `g` has the defining coefficient and root values of `h.lift`, hence the two ring homomorphisms coincide. Taking both realizations to be \(S\), the canonical algebra equivalence is consequently the identity. Thus, in each `Iff`, both propositions can be established independently from the same universal-property lemmas and then paired as equivalent.
